title: A member can file a complaint attributed to any other flat in the society
steps: 1. Sign in as 9000000007 (owner of A-202, QA-T Lotus Society). 2. POST /rest/v1/rpc/file_complaint with p_reporter_flat_id = id of flat A-101 (the chairman's flat), p_kind=society, p_description='QA-T lift not working'. 3. select reporter_flat_id from complaints.
expected: INVALID_FLAT: the reporter flat must be a flat the caller holds an active membership on.
actual: 200 {complaint_id: fc45ddee-...}. complaints row has reporter_id = 9000000007 but reporter_flat_id = A-101. file_complaint only checks that the flat is in the caller's society (flats.society_id = v_society_id), not that the caller lives there. The status trail would show the complaint as coming from A-101.

title: Every resident can read every flat's visitor log, including visitor phone numbers
steps: 1. Guard 9000000006 logs a visit for flat A-201 (guard_create_visit, visitor_phone 9876500000). 2. Sign in as 9000000007 (plain member, flat A-202). 3. GET /rest/v1/visitor_requests?select=visitor_name,visitor_phone,flat_id.
expected: 0 rows: a resident sees only visits for their own flat; managers may see all.
actual: 200 with the A-201 visit, visitor name and phone. RLS policy visitor_requests_secretary_read is USING (society_id = current_society_id()) with no role check, so it admits every member, board member and family member of the society. Committee member 9000000004 also read a visit to A-202 (TC-API-446).

title: A guard cannot resolve an SOS addressed to guards
steps: 1. Member 9000000007 raises SOS with p_audience='watchman'. 2. Guard 9000000006 sees it in security_dashboard.active_sos. 3. Guard calls resolve_sos(p_id).
expected: The guard who responds can mark it handled (or the UI says only the raiser/manager can).
actual: 400 NOT_ALLOWED. Only the raiser or a secretary/co_secretary can resolve; the guard dashboard keeps counting it as active until then.
